hero.title: Students are searching everywhere except the library.
hero.lede: NEXTLIB turns natural questions into relevant academic books, helping students move from scattered searching to confident discovery.

problem.title: Library search has not caught up with student behavior.
problem.body: Interviews across Omani libraries and a 666-response student survey point to the same gap: students need more context, better discovery, and less friction.

points.title: Keyword systems are too rigid
points.body: Most interviewed libraries still rely on basic OPAC keyword search.

points.title: Discovery is happening elsewhere
points.body: Students increasingly turn to AI assistants and general search engines first.

points.title: Facilities do not support discovery
points.body: Without digital guidance, the library becomes a place to sit rather than a place to find.

evidence.title: 11 libraries. One clear pattern.
evidence.body: The interviews show a landscape that is partly digital, but still dominated by manual work, basic OPAC search, and limited recommendation support.
evidence.note: Summary of the interview matrix. The full findings cover cataloging, retrieval, assistance, recommendations, collection development, handling, analytics, and preservation.

survey.title: The evidence is not subtle.
survey.body: Across 666 responses, students describe a search experience that is hard to trust and easy to abandon.
stats: abandoned a search at least occasionally

research.body: We developed the idea as a research paper on NLP-based resource discovery for academic libraries. The work was accepted for conference presentation and is planned for publication in IEEE and indexing in Scopus.
